extracted.intended_audience: attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO; OED staff; parties in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures governing disciplinary proceedings, settlement agreements, findings of misconduct, mitigating/aggravating factors, sanctions (suspension, publication, notice), and reinstatement requirements for attorneys registered before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20(a)(2) and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statutory/regulatory authority to bring and approve proceedings and settlement agreements resolving disciplinary complaints against practitioners registered before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Disciplinary Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorneys registered to practice before the USPTO are subject to the Disciplinary Rules of the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility set forth at 37 C.F.R. § 10.20 et seq.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration number and status determine applicability; misconduct in contexts related to practice before the Office can be addressed under these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreement requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Proposed Settlement Agreement must satisfy the requirements of 37 C.F.R. § 11.26 to resolve disciplinary action by settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parties submit a settlement, the Final Order should set forth stipulated facts, legal conclusions, and agreed upon discipline; settlement becomes basis for public discipline when approved by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited conduct: dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation violates 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples here include falsely stating bar admission status, providing a false bar registration number, and knowingly misrepresenting facts to an employer or others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of misrepresentation as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific misrepresentations (telling employer she had taken/passed/been sworn in and providing a false Illinois Bar registration number) are useable factual bases for a disciplinary finding under the cited rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order details timeline and admissions (hiring interview statements, false sworn-in claim, false registration number, employer confrontation and admission) as supporting the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Mitigating circumstances include: showing great remorse; employer report that the conduct was out-of-character; confirmation that respondent never held herself out as a registered attorney to clients; and that respondent did not work on matters requiring local admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors can lead to leniency in imposing discipline (as demonstrated by the settlement suspension length and other terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedies available
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions can include suspension from practice before the USPTO for a specified period, publication of the Final Order, publication of a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette, and notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, the respondent was suspended for three months; the OED Director shall publish the Final Order in the OED Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette; notice of public discipline and reasons must be given to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public notice obligations (OED Reading Room & Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are posted electronically (provided URL), and public notice is required as part of the discipline process to inform relevant agencies and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures other jurisdictions are informed and may take reciprocal or related action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of record in future proceedings (aggravating/rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of the disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, shall be considered when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and may be used (1) as an aggravating factor in determining future discipline and/or (2) to rebut statements or representations by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior settled matters may increase severity of future sanctions or undermine mitigation in later cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement and post-discipline compliance requirements (37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58 & 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement after suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions set out reporting/publication obligations during and after discipline and the procedural requirements and standards for reinstatement application and review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs arising from the proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements may specify allocation of costs; here, each party bears its own costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification of Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders must be served/mailed to the respondent and a certificate of service included indicating mailing/hand delivery dates and addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural compliance with service requirements is recorded in the decision (certificates of service dated and addressed).
